description: While moe originated as fan slang on Japanese internet forums in the late 1980s and early 1990s to describe a particular kind of parasocial attachment to 2D characters, it especially became a codified art style during the 2000s: one characterized by oversized round eyes, soft facial geometry, diminutive body proportions, and pastel or high-saturation color schemes. The aesthetic is most strongly associated with the "Cute Girls Doing Cute Things" (CGDCT) genre and distinguishes itself from the broader kawaii movement through its deliberate use of specific design features to produce emotional responses in an otaku audience.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Cuteness. innocence. endearing vulnerability, parasocial affection
